Subject: Important: Corvane children's ibuprofen, the SYRINGE is the problem, not the medicine

Hi everyone, Rania here, pharmacist at Cedarbrook. I know a lot of parents are worried this morning, so here is exactly what's going on and what to do.

WHAT IS RECALLED
Corvane Pediatric Ibuprofen Oral Suspension 100 mg/5 mL (berry), 120 mL bottle
Lots CV6114A and CV6114B (expiry 08/2027)

Check the lot number on the bottom of the box. If it's not one of those two lots, this recall doesn't apply to you.

WHAT THE PROBLEM IS
The medicine itself is fine. Corvane confirmed it meets all specifications. It is not contaminated and it is not expired (expiry is 08/2027).

The problem is the dosing syringe in the box. The numbers were printed wrong, and every mark measures double what it says:
- the mark that says 2.5 mL actually measures 5 mL
- the mark that says 5 mL actually measures 10 mL

So if you followed the syringe, your child got about twice the dose you meant to give.

WHAT TO DO NOW
1. Throw out the syringe that came in the box. Please don't use it again.
2. Come get a correctly marked syringe from us. It's free for anyone, and you don't need a receipt. New syringes are arriving this morning before noon. If you'd rather not keep the product, you can return it for a full refund.
3. Once you have a correct syringe, the medicine is OK to use as directed on the label.

IF YOUR CHILD ALREADY HAD A DOSE WITH THE OLD SYRINGE
If you have any doubt about how much your child got, call the Ontario Poison Centre at 1-844-764-7669. They're open 24/7 and they will assess your child based on their weight, how many doses they had and when, and their health. I can't safely judge that for each child over Facebook, so please call them. They're the right people for this.

Don't give another dose until the poison centre or your doctor says it's OK.

CALL 911 OR GO TO EMERGENCY RIGHT AWAY if your child is:
- very sleepy or hard to wake up
- vomiting blood
- not peeing
- having a seizure

ABOUT HOW WE FOUND OUT
We got the recall notice from Corvane on the evening of Nov 6. We pulled the remaining bottles from our shelves the morning of Nov 7 and put up signs on the front door and in the kids' aisle. This product is sold over the counter, so for most of these sales we don't have a name or phone number and had no way to call people directly. That's why we're asking you to share this post. Please pass it on to anyone you know who bought children's ibuprofen from us recently.

EXTRA HOURS FOR EXCHANGES
We're opening extra this Saturday, 10 am to 4 pm, just for syringe exchanges and returns.

Our phones are very busy right now. If you can't get through, please come in, or leave a message and we'll call you back. We're working through all of them.

I'm a parent too and I understand how scary this is. Thank you for your patience while we get everyone sorted.

Rania Haddad, Pharmacist
Cedarbrook Pharmacy, Erin Mills Pkwy
